editorial.headline: Insurance Brokerage: Nationally Open, Not Barred by Bali’s Moratorium
editorial.standfirst: Insurance brokerage for policyholders, insured parties and participants is open to full foreign ownership nationally and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 66222 covers the work of an insurance broker acting on behalf of the policyholder, insured party or participant. In practical terms, it brings together consulting services and/or intermediation in the closing of conventional insurance or sharia insurance, then carries that representative role through the handling of claim settlements. The record includes advisory services and/or brokerage, so the activity may be performed through advice, through intermediation, or through both. In every formulation, its defined position is clear: it acts for and in the name of the policyholder, insured party or participant. The scope states that formulation twice, reinforcing the representative relationship at the centre of the activity. This is therefore a precise description of a service joining insurance placement and claims handling for the represented party.

Registration is open across the listed business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. The record places each of those scales within scope. At the national level, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with maximum foreign ownership at 100%. Put plainly, the national record permits a foreign investor to hold the entire business under this activity. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national setting sits alongside the scale listing: the reference to business scale does not create an alternative foreign-ownership ceiling. The national position is consequently direct—this activity is open to PMA, with no recorded foreign-equity restriction below 100%.

Bali requires its own reading because the record includes an island-wide, permanent moratorium that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. This activity is not blocked. The Bali assessment states that, at the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and is therefore outside the moratorium’s block. Its Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The distinction matters: the moratorium remains the stated provincial rule, but this activity’s recorded risk position means it is not caught by it. No Bali-specific foreign-ownership percentage or partnership condition is recorded. On the evidence provided, the candid conclusion is straightforward: a foreign-owned insurance-brokerage business may be registered nationally with up to 100% foreign ownership, and Bali’s stated moratorium does not bar its PMA registration there.
editorial.pullQuote: The national position is direct: this activity is open to PMA, and Bali’s moratorium does not bar its registration.
